subject.title: fix(browser): keep guarded CDP sockets on validated endpoints [AI]

question: Should explicitly configured Chrome MCP profiles be rejected under restrictive CDP policy when Chrome MCP cannot carry OpenClaw's validated DNS lookup, or should the product preserve the attachment path through a separately designed compatibility mechanism?
rationale: This is an intentional security-versus-upgrade behavior choice: the transport cannot currently prove that Chrome MCP reuses the validated lookup, but rejecting existing restricted configurations changes an operator-visible workflow.

options.title: Accept fail-closed Chrome MCP behavior
options.body: Keep the rejection under explicit restrictive policy, document the migration to the OpenClaw driver or host-local profile, and prove both allowed and rejected cases.

options.title: Design a compatibility path
options.body: Preserve existing Chrome MCP attachment only if an owner-approved mechanism can bind or independently validate its actual transport endpoint without weakening the restriction.

options.title: Limit this PR to socket propagation
options.body: Defer Chrome MCP policy changes to a separate product/security decision and land only the Browser transport paths that can carry the validated lookup.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed Chrome MCP behavior
recommendation.body: Keep the rejection under explicit restrictive policy, document the migration to the OpenClaw driver or host-local profile, and prove both allowed and rejected cases.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans Browser profile transport capability, endpoint policy, and the user-visible failure mode for existing Chrome MCP profiles.
